steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on estimating gait parameters from single-camera RGB videos with a Transformer-based network. Motivate clinical gait analysis, explain the limits of current motion capture setups and of video-based pose estimation, and end with our method and a list of contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. Movement-related diseases and why gait analysis matters
2. Current workflow: optical motion capture and its drawbacks
3. Single-camera video and pose estimation as an alternative
4. Proposed two-stage spatio-temporal Transformer
5. Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Motivation
- approx. 1.7 billion people worldwide affected by movement-related diseases
- wide range of diseases harming muscles, bones, joints
- cognitive function associated with manner of movement
- -> human gait analysis crucial for early diagnosis of musculoskeletal conditions
- clinical gait analysis: quantitatively measure general gait parameters (walking speed, cadence, gait deviation index (GDI)) -> overall health/function of gait

2. Optical motion capture (Mocap)
- multiple specialized cameras + sensors track patient movements
- 2D videos constructed into 3D motion data -> compute gait parameters
- drawbacks: expensive equipment, well-trained personnel, careful calibration and positioning
- alternatives: wearable inertial sensors, depth cameras; limited accessibility (cost, specialized skills)

3. Single-camera video
- recently: 2D markerless video sequences from single-camera videos; convenient, economical, less need for expensive equipment
- pose estimation models learn/extract 2D skeletal data for gait assessment
- estimating gait parameters directly from skeletal data error-prone: pose tracking lacks robustness, precision
- deep neural networks: expressive, resilient to noise -> more efficient, precise estimation

4. Our method
- novel spatio-temporal Transformer for gait analysis from single-camera RGB videos
- learns intricate spatio-temporal dynamics of gait (hard for traditional methods)
- stage 1: OpenPose extracts 2D pose keypoints from video
- stage 2: spatio-temporal Transformer predicts Gait Deviation Index, knee flexion angle at maximum extension, speed, cadence

5. Contributions
- first spatio-temporal Transformer for quantitative gait parameter estimation from single-view RGB videos; spatial + temporal features from anatomical keypoints
- flexible network -> beats state of the art, fewer parameters, no manually crafted time series
- code + trained models public: https://github.com/vinuni-vishc/transformer-gait-analysis

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Around 1.7 billion people worldwide are currently affected by movement-related diseases. These are a wide range of diseases that have a negative impact on the muscles, bones and joints. A person's cognitive function has also been shown to be related to the way they move. Because of this, human gait analysis has become a crucial tool for diagnosing musculoskeletal conditions early. In clinical gait analysis it is essential to quantitatively measure general gait parameters like walking speed, cadence or gait deviation index (GDI), since they determine the overall health and function of a patient's gait.

Today the workflow of human motion analysis usually relies on optical motion capture systems (Mocap). These systems need several specialized cameras and sensors to track how the patient moves. The two-dimensional (2D) videos from the cameras are then constructed into three-dimensional (3D) motion data, and this data can then be used to compute different gait parameters. The problem is that Mocap systems need expensive equipment and well-trained personnel, and they also need careful calibration and positioning of the system to perform well. Wearable inertial sensors or depth cameras are alternatives, but they are not very accessible either, because of their cost and the specialized skills needed to operate them.

- recently: 2D markerless video sequences from single-camera videos, convenient + economical, less need for expensive equipment
- pose estimation models learn/extract 2D skeletal data for gait assessment
- but gait parameters directly from skeletal data -> errors (pose tracking not robust/precise)
- deep neural networks (expressive, resilient to noise) -> more efficient, precise estimation
- our method: spatio-temporal Transformer for single-camera RGB videos; learns intricate spatio-temporal gait dynamics (hard for traditional methods)
- stage 1: OpenPose 2D keypoints; stage 2: Transformer predicts Gait Deviation Index, knee flexion angle at maximum extension, speed, cadence
- contributions: first spatio-temporal Transformer for this from single-view RGB videos; beats state of the art with fewer parameters, no manually crafted time series; code + models at https://github.com/vinuni-vishc/transformer-gait-analysis

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Around 1.7 billion people worldwide are currently affected by movement-related diseases. These are a wide range of diseases that have a negative impact on the muscles, bones and joints. A person's cognitive function has also been shown to be related to the way they move. Because of this, human gait analysis has become a crucial tool for diagnosing musculoskeletal conditions early. In clinical gait analysis it is essential to quantitatively measure general gait parameters like walking speed, cadence or gait deviation index (GDI), since they determine the overall health and function of a patient's gait.

Today the workflow of human motion analysis usually relies on optical motion capture systems (Mocap). These systems need several specialized cameras and sensors to track how the patient moves. The two-dimensional (2D) videos from the cameras are then constructed into three-dimensional (3D) motion data, and this data can then be used to compute different gait parameters. The problem is that Mocap systems need expensive equipment and well-trained personnel, and they also need careful calibration and positioning of the system to perform well. Wearable inertial sensors or depth cameras are alternatives, but they are not very accessible either, because of their cost and the specialized skills needed to operate them.

Recently, 2D markerless video sequences captured from single-camera videos have become a convenient and economical option because they reduce the need for expensive equipment. Pose estimation models in particular have become a powerful tool for automatically learning and extracting 2D skeletal data for assessing human gait. But estimating gait parameters directly from this skeletal data tends to have errors, because pose tracking algorithms are not robust and precise enough. So deep neural networks, which are expressive and resilient to noise, can be a more efficient and precise way to estimate general gait parameters.

In this study we propose a new spatio-temporal Transformer architecture for gait analysis with single-camera RGB videos. It can learn the intricate spatio-temporal dynamics of human gait effectively, which is a challenge for most traditional methods. The architecture has two stages. The first stage extracts the 2D human pose keypoints from a video with OpenPose. The second stage uses a spatio-temporal Transformer network to predict the gait parameters, which are Gait Deviation Index, knee flexion angle at maximum extension, speed and cadence. Our main contributions are the following:

- We are the first to use a spatio-temporal Transformer network to estimate gait parameters quantitatively for gait analysis from single-view RGB videos. The network design lets us extract both spatial and temporal features from the anatomical keypoints taken from single-camera RGB videos.

- Because the proposed network is flexible, it does better than current state-of-the-art methods at predicting gait parameters, while also having fewer parameters and not needing manually crafted time series.

- Our code and trained deep learning models are publicly available: https://github.com/vinuni-vishc/transformer-gait-analysis.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Approximately 1.7 billion individuals worldwide are currently affected by movement-related diseases [1]. These conditions cover a wide range of diseases that negatively impact the muscles, bones, and joints. A person's cognitive function has also been shown to be associated with their manner of movement [2]. As a result, human gait analysis has become a crucial tool for the early diagnosis of musculoskeletal conditions. In clinical gait analysis, quantitatively measuring general gait parameters such as walking speed, cadence, or gait deviation index (GDI) is essential for determining the overall health and function of a patient's gait [3,4,5].

The current workflow of human motion analysis typically relies on optical motion capture systems (Mocap) [6]. These systems use multiple specialized cameras and sensors to track the patient's movements. The two-dimensional (2D) videos from these cameras are then constructed into three-dimensional (3D) motion data [7], which can be used to compute various gait parameters. Unfortunately, Mocap systems require expensive equipment and well-trained personnel, and they demand careful calibration and positioning for optimal performance [8]. Alternatives include wearable inertial sensors or depth cameras [9,10], but their accessibility is limited by their cost and the specialized skills required to operate them.

Recently, 2D markerless video sequences captured from single-camera videos have emerged as a convenient and economical option [11] that minimizes the need for expensive equipment. In particular, pose estimation models have become a powerful tool to automatically learn and extract 2D skeletal data [12] for human gait assessment [13]. However, estimating gait parameters directly from these skeletal data is prone to errors due to the limited robustness and precision of pose tracking algorithms [14]. The expressiveness and resilience to noise of deep neural networks therefore make them a more efficient and precise method for estimating general gait parameters [15]. In this study, we propose a novel spatio-temporal Transformer architecture for gait analysis using single-camera RGB videos, which can effectively learn the intricate spatio-temporal dynamics of human gait, a challenge for most traditional methods. The first stage of the architecture extracts 2D human pose keypoints from a video using OpenPose [12]. The second stage uses a spatio-temporal Transformer network to predict gait parameters, including Gait Deviation Index, knee flexion angle at maximum extension, speed, and cadence. Our main contributions are summarized as follows:

- • We are the first to introduce a spatio-temporal Transformer network for quantitatively estimating gait parameters from single-view RGB videos. Our network design extracts both spatial and temporal features effectively from the anatomical keypoints taken from single-camera RGB videos.

- • The flexibility of the proposed network helps it achieve superior performance in predicting gait parameters compared to current state-of-the-art methods, while reducing the number of parameters and removing the need for manually crafted time series.

- • Our code and trained deep learning models are publicly available: https://github.com/vinuni-vishc/transformer-gait-analysis.
